title: Normal-flat normal cone and linear vertex at a Hilbert--Samuel near point
statement:
Let $X$ be a reduced scheme of finite type over $\mathbf Q$, locally closed in a smooth scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For a point $z$ of a scheme $W$ of finite type over $\mathbf Q$ (below $W=X$ or $W=X'$), set $h_{W,z}(n)=\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{W,z}/\mathfrak m_z^{n+1})$ and $H_{W,z}=\Lambda^{\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbf Q}\kappa(z)}h_{W,z}$, where $\Lambda f(n)=\sum_{j=0}^n f(j)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-length, def-kun-transcendence-degree, def-weil-residue-field]. Let $C\hookrightarrow X$ be a smooth closed subscheme on which $z\mapsto H_{X,z}$ is locally constant. Let $\pi:X'\to X$ be the blowup of $C$, equivalently the scheme-theoretic strict transform of $X$ in the ambient blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup, def-nagata-strict-transform]. Fix $y\in X'$ over $x\in C$ with $H_{X',y}=H_{X,x}$. Put $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_x$, $I=\mathcal I_{C,x}$, $A=R/I$, $k=R/\mathfrak m$, and $G=\operatorname{gr}_I R=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}I^j/I^{j+1}$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring]. Then $G$ is flat over $A$ (tensoring with $G$ preserves injections of $A$-modules). Identify the exceptional fibre over $x$ with $\operatorname{Proj}(G\otimes_A k)$ [def-pc-proj, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. There exist a standard graded $k$-algebra $B$ [def-pc-standard-graded-algebra], an integer $e\ge1$, and a graded isomorphism
$$G\otimes_A k\simeq B[T_1,\ldots,T_e],\qquad \deg T_i=1,$$
where the polynomial algebra is that of [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], such that $y$ lies in the closed projective linear subspace defined by $B_+=\bigoplus_{j>0}B_j$, namely $\operatorname{Proj}(k[T_1,\ldots,T_e])$. No rationality or closedness assumption on $x$ or $y$ is imposed.

source.place: VIII 2.3.13, printed p.94, synchronization input; precise lower results: Bennett normal-flatness criterion and characteristic-zero Hironaka near-point theorem. WANTED archival copy: Cossart--Jannsen--Saito, Canonical embedded and non-embedded resolution of singularities for excellent two-dimensional schemes, March 12 2009 preprint, Theorems 2.2--2.3 and 2.14, printed pp.28--29,36 (these preliminary theorems have no dimension-two restriction), https://epub.uni-regensburg.de/13766/1/MP32.pdf. The polynomial description is the linear directrix of the normal-cone fibre; no Stacks tag states the near-point theorem. For the raw near condition use Lambda^delta h_y=h_x, delta=trdeg_{kappa(x)}kappa(y), as in the Bennett/Hironaka formulation, not an unproved identification with the differently normalized component-dependent H in CJS. CJS Theorem 2.14 cites Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities, Theorem IV, and Additive groups associated with points of a projective space, Theorem 2; these originals are WANTED too.

proof.text: Apply the already stated nonreduced near-point normal-cone theorem [lem-per-scheme-near-point-normal-cone] to the same p, i, c, hconstant, z, y, hy and hnear. It has exactly the required normal-flatness, monomial-specified exceptional-fibre pullback, and polynomial directrix conclusions; it does not require reducedness, so the extra reducedness hypothesis here is harmless. The five common constructions have been moved verbatim into their own definition module to make this specialization acyclic.

Source: I fetched the CJS 2009 preprint and read Def 2.1, Thm 2.2(2)(ii), Thm 2.3 (Bennett (1)⇔(2)), Lemma 2.4, Thm 2.10(2) and the proof of 2.14. That proof gives Hironaka's homogeneous subgroup scheme B_{P,x'} with x' ∈ P(B) and an action on the cone, in any characteristic. With h = ΛH^(0), the raw forms h_x = Λ^d h_η and Λ^δ h_y = h_x are exactly the CJS criteria. Steps 2 and 4 derive them from the Λ^{trdeg_Q} normalization through t_η = t_x + d and the trdeg tower, and the cited nodes say what the steps take from them. Step 5: fibre degree j is I^j/mI^j = (I^j/I^{j+1})⊗k, since I^{j+1} ⊆ mI^j. Step 6 rules out a component inside the centre: minimal prime ⇒ R_I a field ⇒ torsion in the flat G ⇒ I = I² ⇒ Nakayama ⇒ I = 0 ⇒ empty Proj. Steps 8–9 (characteristic 0): the (1, r−1) bidegree argument plus Euler gives L = (L_1), and Hasse–Taylor gives K = J[T]; e ≥ 1 follows from L ⊆ q_y. Bennett node: it allows I minimal, which CJS 2.1 excludes; I checked it stays true there (flat ⇒ I = 0 by the Step 6 argument; equality ⇒ I contains all minimal primes by CJS Lemma 2.4 ⇒ I = 0).
